utterances.text: Let's look at what you told the investigators when you were interviewed. It appears at some length. Paragraph 5 of the statement, which is still up but not being broadcast. We are going to the English at page 2 and the B/C/S at page 4. Now, in these paragraphs, you tell the tragic story of the death of your son. It's a little different from what you told the Court today. Let's read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's page 5 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I think in the e-court actually -- my apologies. Absolutely right. It's page 5 in the e-court in English, and page 4 of the B/C/S, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to not read out the names: My mother came out of the house carrying my son, child from my first marriage. As she was coming down the stairs, when she was on the second stair holding him in her arms I saw - this is a person I'm not going to name - approaching my mother and placing a rifle barrel against my son's head and fired it so that he killed both my mother and son by one bullet. The child fell out of her arms from the impact of the shot and the bullet hit my mother in her chest causing her to fall off the stairs. Other than myself, my father, someone else and a woman were observing this. So you describe this event in some detail and you note that your father also witnessed the manner in which your son was killed. Now, was that the truth that you told on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, my father was not a witness to this, nor was he able to see. That's two. Three: A moment ago I told you also that I heard a shot fired from a rifle but I didn't see by who. And this name you actually didn't mention, that name features in the statement in my evidence today and yesterday. He was on the spot, and he's the man who knows best about the way my mother was murdered. And with that man -- I had an agreement with that man many years later because once he had saved my life and another time I saved his life. When somebody gives you your life as a gift, whereas he could have killed you, it's a great gift.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the last sentence about 48 hours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You also see the name and surname of another person who lives in Holland here. You can bring him, I'll sit over there on that side. And if you want me, I'll tell you his name, the man who was there and who has been living in Holland for I don't know how many years. The man who was brought to Visoko together with me for an exchange, you can bring him as well. Muhamed Ahmetovic, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: So you now say your father didn't witness this event but other than that, this is your account of your son's tragic death?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ma'am, I don't know about my father, whether he was ever there. All I know is that when I saw him, when I lived with him for a couple of months, he told me somebody had visited him at the house, at his house, and he refused to talk to that person. But I had even greater problems because he wasn't willing to talk, he wasn't willing to tell the truth. Whenever I mention about the things that had happened, including the murder of my mother, he says: I don't know about it. I won't talk about it. I don't know what kind of agreement he had made with Bajro Kulovac, but I have other witnesses. I once came to see him with a woman who had been a witness to this but he wasn't willing to discuss it even then. He has a new child, a new wife. He was enjoying benefits that I was dead. He went to Tuzla, then he came back to pick up his things. He said you can't live here any more, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Pack, please ask your question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your father --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Don't talk about father, yes. But she asked about your son's death. What you stated in the statement is correct? That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, listen to me carefully, listen carefully to what I'm going to tell you. You have that statement that I gave yesterday. Can I say the name and surname of that man? When the man invited me and said that he would have a drink, that's his brother. That's the younger brother. And this story is about the elder brother. Since we had an agreement, you will let me go, you will let me live, I'm not going to deal with this case, nobody is going to arrest this man, if I'm able to forgive that, I, who have suffered the most, and I don't want this discussed, the matter of my mother and son, I want you to bring this Ahmed -- Muhamed Ahmetovic. He lives here in Holland.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you say something, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: There is problem with transcript. The whole sentence is missing from the page 61, line 15 and 16, witness said that his father didn't want to tell the truth. It is not recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It is in a couple of lines before that, line 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters are telling us that it's in -- already in the transcript, line 16. Yes. Please continue, Ms. Pack.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'm still not clear, Witness, that you answered my question. This account that you give here in the statement, this very detailed account of the circumstances of your son's death, which you saw, do you say this is true?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ma'am, you have really decided to make me look like an idiot.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Witness, I just want you to answer the question, okay?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to discuss this. I let that man go free. He's living his own life. He offered me my life in exchange, and end of story. End of story about this document. I don't want to hear one more word about it. And don't make me talk here and make me look like a fool. I've told you, all these papers regarding this statement are not a problem but I don't want to judge this man. When I was telling the truth, you should have come for me then and brought me here. When I was telling the truth, I was getting only threats in return. Why have you not been looking for me, Madam?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm asking for a break. I cannot listen to you anymore. You are trying to depict me like I don't know what. Let's go to the lie detector. I need a break and I need a cigarette. In all over the world, everybody has the right to a break now and then.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Witness, you are not answering this question because unbelievably you lied about the circumstances of your own son's death.

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered you yesterday and I wasn't lying about my son's death. I did not want to mention the name of that man. That's the only problem. I told you a moment ago, when you asked me, that we were getting out from the basement and my mother and my son were also coming out of the house. I didn't see that man. I just did not want to mention his name. I don't -- I want a cigarette. I don't want to go on a hunger strike here. I didn't go on a hunger strike even when things were much worse for me. I was telling the truth. People were writing it down on a computer. I told you I was the last in the column of people coming out of the basement. I heard the shot. I didn't see the man, so I don't want to mention that man. This written on this paper, it means that I saw the man who was shooting but I don't want to mention him. You can repeat the lie detector test. I just didn't want to mention the man who shot, who fired that shot. You know what, if you don't let me out of here, I'm going to light one here. I am inviting, I'm calling this witness, Muhamed Ahmetovic, to come here because he was there and he saw it better than anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm stopping you, Mr. Witness. If you have further questions, we will take a break, Ms. Pack.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, just a few more. I won't be long, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How long?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'll aim to wrap it up in 15 or 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll take a break then. We will have a break for 45 minutes and resume at quarter past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Shall we continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: After your release from prison, you went to the offices of the State Investigation and Protection Agency, SIPA. You went there on the 16th of March, 2010; right?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam Prosecutor, you should ask me how I got to SIPA in 2010. It wasn't of my own accord, 2010.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'd like to bring up a statement, an official record, please, it's 65 ter 25500. Shouldn't be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: This is an official record of an interview with you on the 16th of March, 2010, a SIPA official record. And I'm going to read out what it says, I'll be careful not to identify you. If Mr. Robinson is concerned about me reading any of the paragraphs specifically, then I'd be grateful if he would let me know in advance as we go through. So the first paragraph, just to summarise it, you came voluntarily to the offices of the State Investigation and Protection Agency, gives the address, on 16th of March, 2010. He was accompanied by Alagic, Damir, attorney at law, whose offices and so on. Damir Alagic is your lawyer, right, was your lawyer?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, who ruined my life.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You've been making these allegations today and in your statement and previously, he hit you, he beat you with the investigator who interviewed you in 2008. We've heard that. Let's just go on with this. Witness stated that the reason why he wanted to talk to members of SIPA was the fact that he was engaged by lawyer Goran Petronijevic as a Defence witness for The Hague defendant Radovan Karadzic, immediately after his release from prison on the 12th of March, 2010. Witness was instructed what and how to testify in written form. That's the allegation you made to SIPA on the 16th of March, 2010; right?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Well, let's see how it goes on. We will jump the next paragraph, we'll go down to the last one on that page in the English, it's same page in the B/C/S, it's the fourth paragraph in the B/C/S. A few -- talks about a discussion in the warden's office in the prison, a certain correctional officer told you that some people who wished to talk to you had arrived. She told witness that she had written authorisation that they can talk to him and that people in question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we please have the reference in B/C/S so we can precisely read what you are reading from to the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: My apologies to the interpreter. It's the fourth paragraph of that page that you see on the screen. I just paraphrased it a little. But I'm going to read it now directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it fourth paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Fourth paragraph refers to 12th of March, 2010. But I don't see such date in the fourth paragraph in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: That's the fifth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, fourth, I see. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, so the fourth paragraph, I paraphrased it a little. And then we go over the page in English, please, to page 2 and stay on the same page in the B/C/S. That's the fourth paragraph in the B/C/S on the first page, that is when Petronijevic, Goran, came to visit him with another person whom witness did not know. On that occasion, Goran allegedly told witness that he would be released and that he would ensure witness was protected from threats from Bosniaks, that Goran would change witness's name and that he would get him papers on the name of - I won't read out the name - that witness would initially be taken to Serbia and that after his testimony he would be returned to a third country - I won't name the third country - from where he had been deported and where his wife and daughter lived. They talked to him --

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, I don't have a daughter.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Is that the only area which you disagree with here? The rest is accurate, is it?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want you to show me the rest, please feel free to go on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: They talked to him from 11.00 in the morning until 19.30. The interview was allegedly recorded by an audio recorder. They said that he had been in Srebrenica the entire time. They said that he should talk about the events in Srebrenica, particularly about the events after the fall of Srebrenica. They told him that he needed to co-operate with them in full. Next paragraph. Witness was released from prison on the 12th of March, 2010, and was met by three persons at the parking lot in front of the gate. These persons were lawyer, Petronijevic, Goran, and another two persons unfamiliar to him. They told him to get into the car with him. The vehicle was a red Golf 2. He did not remember, et cetera. It goes on. As soon as they arrived - this is the place where you were taken to, perhaps it's better not to read it out - the two persons who accompanied Petronijevic took him to the police station where witness regularly reported to the police. Witness was obliged to do so because of his conditional release. Witness stated that all police officers were familiar with the two persons accompanying him and that everyone said hello to them. After they had left the police station, witness was allegedly taken to Motel Peric - I won't say where that was - where he was met in room 33 which was on the second floor. He spent the night alone in the room. In the morning he was picked up by the same person. It goes on. A lot of detail about this -- this -- the circumstances of your stay in this motel. And I'll just go on to the following page in the English, and I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I think you're going slightly too fast for the French translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Witness spent the night in that apartment. In the morning of the next day, Goran Petronijevic and these two other persons came to the apartment. Goran brought quite a few pieces of A4 format printouts. Goran told witness to read those pages, to study and memorise what was written as he would need to testify in relation to what was said in the text. Goran also told witness that he would be taken to Belgrade on Wednesday where he would give testimony at the prosecutor's office. Before they had left, witness requested a TV set or a radio, and so on. I'll leave the next paragraph, a few more details. And then we get to tomorrow morning, that is on the 15th of March, 2010, Goran Petronijevic and these two other persons came to the apartment again. Petronijevic brought a voice recorder and posed questions to witness. Petronijevic would then show him with his finger which portion of the printed text he should read. The witness allegedly read out parts of text shown to him by Petronijevic. The witness stated that he remembers that his name and general information which he read were written at the beginning of the text, the rest of the text and the questions had to do with the column which headed towards Tuzla after the fall of Srebrenica. The questions had to do with whether or not Muslims killed each other, whether they opened fire on Serbs. He replied to these questions by reading the text from the printouts according to which Muslims did kill each other. He was then asked about Naser Oric, Tursunovic and others, and he read out prepared answers. The interview took about two hours. Goes on. Following page in the English, after the interview was over, Petronijevic and those two other persons left the apartment, told them he can go out, but that he should be careful not to be recognised. And then apparently before he left the apartment, he - that's you - hid a number of pages given to him by Goran under the drawer and underneath the oven in the apartment while the rest of the pages remained on and underneath the table. Then you go on later, he phoned Alagic, Damir, the lawyer who previously represented him in the murder case, goes on to describe your movements, and then the lawyer -- then you check in with your lawyer. In the end you say -- in your last paragraph you say -- at the end, the witness stated that the information in his statement given to the SIPA representatives was incorrect but that he had given such a statement because of the fact that the interview was conducted in the offices of the prison where he did not feel safe. It goes on. So, these allegations, these are allegations you made about Goran Petronijevic to SIPA when you got out of prison because you thought that these allegations might finally get you the attention of the BiH state authorities and SIPA; right?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Madam. I just have a wish for you to give me an answer. Who is the man who wrote this? (redacted)

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) I would want to see him so that he could say before all of you when it was that I gave this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Could we go back to private session briefly?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, this person that signed this statement and wrote it, I never sat with this man, never had coffee with him, never talked to him. That is one thing. And now, also, what is mentioned here, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Ms. Pack.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Well, Witness, you now lie and say you didn't make these allegations and you cover yourself, don't you, with this story about being beaten up by the SIPA investigation and by your own lawyer; right? Covering yourself, covering the first lie.

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, I never said that Damir Alagic beat me. What I said was that I was beaten by Bajro Kulovac in his presence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Well, it's a matter for the record but you said earlier today that he hit you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'd like to admit this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bajro Kulovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we will receive it under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives Exhibit P6560 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Then you went on to report your story to the press, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 25435.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not to be broadcast, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: This is not to be broadcast, obviously.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Wait for my question, please. So you went to the press with your lawyer and you reported your story about Goran Petronijevic, the story that would give you the notoriety you were seeking; right?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you straight away about the press. You see this picture here? You see this Damir Alagic sitting there? Do you know where this picture was taken and how it was taken? Now, Damir Alagic wanted to present me to the public in a certain way, just to cover up the fact that I left Bijeljina, disappeared from Bijeljina. As far as I know, about this press and all the rest, what was happening in SIPA, according to my information, you in The Hague did know about that and my life was in danger at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Let's just look at this story, shall we? So its title we can see: How Karadzic's attorney recruit witnesses. You say they changed my name so that I could testify in The Hague, and then you've got a long paragraph, and it basically duplicates your allegations that you made when you voluntarily attended SIPA's offices. It repeats those allegations. So in the second paragraph, it says, witness -- the witness, whom the RS Supreme Court testified to five years in prison for allegedly killing a Bosniak from Srebrenica in 1995, goes on to say what the lawyer says about that, your lawyer, supporting your claims, says we are supposed to testify in The Hague under a new identity that numerous killed men from Srebrenica were actually alive or that the Muslims themselves had killed them. And then he goes on to describe your account, and we can see that here in the English on the first page, and then we can go over. It basically duplicates what you said to SIPA. We can go over in the English to the following page. Under the heading: He was learning names, it says: Following this, the witness continues, an attorney visited him every day and brought in papers which he had to learn by heart. It quotes you: I had to know but heart the names of 36 Muslim who are listed as killed in Srebrenica whom I would testify to in Belgrade and in The Hague that they were alive or that the Muslims had killed them. However, whilst breaking my fingers and drawing crosses on my body, they did manage to extract a confession from me for something I hadn't done once they won't ever again. Seem to be alleging there that these lawyers, Dr. Karadzic's lawyers, were drawing crosses on you. I'm not going anywhere from the federation, the witness told us, who managed to escape, and so on. There we are. This was the story you gave to the press; right?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not right, Madam. Damir Alagic, when they took this picture of me, he went to this radio television, wherever this paper is from, and they gave that interview and they rigged all of it. That is one thing. Number two, the Defence - how do I put this? - Karadzic's attorneys they never cut me. They never beat me. They did not ask me to do anything by force. I was cut in Bratunac, in the camp, on the 10th of May, 1992. What they wanted, not from -- they didn't want me to speak about that ever. And then Damir Alagic, they put this here so that they could all launder this - and how do I put this? - to have this case removed. When I was brought from the police in Sarajevo by Bajro Kulovac and Damir Alagic they frisked me and they found a calling card in my pocket, a few cigarettes, a telephone, a lighter, and also I had problems with that telephone. The main co-ordinator knows that. How do I put this? The Karadzic Defence main co-ordinator, when the police in my native town protected me. For this statement, and for the statement at that moment, you were informed about that, you in the Prosecutor's office in The Hague, you were informed what was being done to me, what was happening to me. Through the public, Damir Alagic tried to remove me, just so that I wouldn't reach you and then you, here, from The Hague, called and you did what I said in my statement, that Damir Alagic called me on the phone and said The Hague is looking for you, do not contact them by any means until I arrive there, and I will take care of all of that. Madam, so all of this is what I refer to in my statement. All of this was rigged. I was framed. And I've been saying that yesterday and today. Sorry, Judge, I was informed in those moments when I was brought to SIPA, to this main director there, and I said that in my statement, that the director, the main director of SIPA asked me whether I was forced to - how do I explain this to you? - did I say this because I was forced to or did I do it of my own free will in Bijeljina to Nebojsa Jovanovic, Prosecutor, or did I do that voluntarily? And I said that in my statement and when I tried to say to him, to this director of SIPA, that I was not forced to provide anything, and it's contained in my statement, and then Damir Alagic put his hand on my left shoulder and he said I'll take care of all of that. I was then taken out of SIPA and I was outside for two days until I was found by another man who knew me from Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Witness, wait, wait, wait. You had your photo taken for the papers; right? This is a photo of you taken for the press on the 16th, 17th of March; right?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a photo, but are you wondering how come I'm sitting next to Damir Alagic in this photo? Look better. Took the original of the paper and you will see that we are talking about two different snapshots, two different photos. And they were rigged. And Damir Alagic wanted to do his utmost not to have him here. You know, you're a Prosecutor and the co-ordinator is familiar with the case because at the time he also had problems because the article was about him as well. They searched me, they found his visit card, his calling card, and Damir Alagic composed all this based on that calling card because he wanted to prevent me from contacting this gentleman whom you can see. Damir Alagic took that calling card from me and he said, I'll deal with that, to prevent me from contacting that gentlemen. When I was beaten, when I was in prison, when my life was destroyed in Sarajevo in the federation, at that time, I used all the means to get in touch with somebody in order to survive because I had been threatened. Perhaps eight or nine months later, when I found out that --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Just wait, please. Wait, wait, Witness. You're lying. When you --

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I'm lying. Bring Damir Alagic here and then we'll see who is lying.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: When you attended SIPA's offices in March 2010, you were still trying to figure out, weren't you, if you could get anything out of him, right, if they could be your route to testifying in the state court or The Hague, and then you realised, didn't you, that they had investigated your claims and they didn't believe them.

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And did they find any papers on the desk? Who was it who investigated? Did they find anything, any papers, under that cooker in the apartment where I allegedly was? Did they find any papers, if they indeed carried out that investigation? Was anything found?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Witness, you made the decision, didn't you, that Dr. Karadzic's team were your route to The Hague; right? So you piled claim upon preposterous claim, depending on who you were talking to. You signed a statement full of lies and you've come here today to lie to these Judges; right?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not correct. Judges, you have that in my statement and what I have been saying since yesterday. And I stand by my words. I stand by the statement that I provided in the country from which I have arrived here. And as for what you said about my mother and my son, I repeated what is on paper already. And I asked the main co-ordinator to release that person and that person should not be touched by anybody. I mentioned their names at the time. I was telling the truth, I was telling the truth about the murder of my mother and my son, but I don't want that person to be touched, to be arrested or tried. And as for what Damir Alagic did and the document that you showed me that was signed by Ejub Zukic, those things were rigged by them in the federation. They wanted at all cost to clear their names and they wanted to blame Karadzic's Defence for everybody. That's number one. And number two, Madam, let me tell you: I am here and I have fought for -- against such thieves and such truths for 17 years. I wanted you to help me as a Prosecutor, I wanted to arrange a meeting with these people with your mediation, before you. And then, only then, will you be able to see and hear who is telling the truth and who is lying.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I have no further questions, but I'd like to ask for the report to be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You're not tendering the interview or statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'm grateful. I thought I'd asked for that to be admitted. Yes I'd like to have both of those admitted, please. It's the 65 ter 25500, the record, and the news report, 254 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about 25520? 2008.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I wanted just to have the page. Yes, please, Your Honour. We rose rather quickly, and, I'm sorry, I should have dealt with that when we returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not recommending you to tender but I'm just checking.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'm grateful. If I could just have that page that I read out which was the -- which I can identify for the Registrar, 65 ter 25520, it was page 5 of the English and B/C/S page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'll hear from Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And then of this 25500, I'd like to have that all admitted, please. It's substantially read through, but I would like to have it admitted, and, furthermore, the report, 25435. Apologies for doing it all at once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You answered all -- with respect to all of those items.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I did, Mr. President, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will receive them all.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 25520 receives Exhibit P6561 under seal, 65 ter number 25435 receives Exhibit P6562 under seal, and 65 ter number 25500 was already admitted as Exhibit P6560 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Excellencies. I want to clarify some things that we heard during the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, earlier yesterday it was suggested to you by the Prosecutor that you had decided to tell the truth after having decided to talk to my Defence team and then you got in touch with my Defence team. When did you decide to tell the truth and to shed light on everything that you know about the crimes?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I never at any point did I ever suggest to the witness that he ever told the truth, perhaps once a very long time ago. I really -- this has no connection with my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, such wordings in the Prosecutor's questions happen every day. In their questions, there are a lot of suggestions and allegations that you don't allow me to correct at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just come to your question. What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is this: Did you decide to tell the truth, did you decide to testify - let's not mention the word truth - after having got in touch with my Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: He's putting words into the witness's mouth. Totally inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, please, the Prosecutor suggested --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, probably you may ask Mr. Robinson how to formulate your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is just a follow-up on the Prosecutor's allegation and that was that the witness decided to use my Defence team in order to be put in the position to testify, and that that was why he testifies the way he does. I'm asking him whether that is the fact, and, if not, when was it that he decided to speak out and to testify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since 1996, when I was in that office where I was detained -- when I was detained, ever since then I have wanted to come here and to tell you what I have been telling you so far. However, the -- some individuals from the federation prevented me from coming here earlier. I'm not here only because of you. I'm not here only to be seen by somebody or even by this Tribunal or this Bench, I'm here of my own accord and I have managed to do that. I am a happy man. I wanted to come here when Naser was here but then a search warrant was issued against me and I was prevented from coming here. Ever since then, from 2003 or 2004, things have been happening, and I have suffered the brunt of those things, all in order to prevent me from saying what had happened, and this is what I said in my statement, that there are people who will come here and who will confirm my story. However, these people are now looking at me because they know what happened to me at the hands of Bajro Kulovac, and those are the leaders of the SDA and the Mothers of Srebrenica. Now they are all looking with their eyes wide open at me to see how you will react when you see such a strong witness as me. The documents that the Prosecutor presented and showed to you, my only wish is for these people to come here and look me in the eyes, eyeball to eyeball, to see when and how they recorded all those things, when they wrote all those statements. I'm not looking for anything else from you, the International Criminal Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up D4181 in e-court. And could it not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's D4181.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: He's talked about this picture.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yeah, maybe 82, 4182. [Interpretation] Not to be broadcast as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When did you meet my legal adviser?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the month exactly. It was sometime in January or February.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: D4182, not to be broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When did you write this letter to the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have been through this in direct examination and in cross-examination. I just can't see how anything new can have arisen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it not too early to object? You cross-examined about this document. And just he asked as a beginning the date of the document. Let's see how it goes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, Judge, it says very clearly that it was written on the 11th of April, 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know anybody from my team at the time?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, on page 101, line 22, this is for the other participants, you stated this: Damir Alagic brought me to SIPA. Earlier today in both the questions and the SIPA documents, it says that you went to SIPA voluntarily. Did you?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I stand by the statement that I gave here and to your co-ordinator. I can give you his name. I repeat that I was forcibly taken to Sandici, from there to the Kladanj, to the police, by car, to Damir Alagic and then Damir Alagic took me and went -- me to SIPA, Bakir Izetbegovic was there as well as Naser Oric. And there I stated that Naser Oric did not beat me there, he just provoked me, he called me traitor, and so on and so forth. And when that was finished, Bajro Kulovac came and then he took me to SIPA. From the first police station, there I was searched, and there they found the calling card of your co-ordinator. It was in my pocket, and Damir Alagic immediately took it and said he would deal with that. Why is that? Because I had provided a statement in 2010, I don't remember when, whether it was in January or February, to your Defence team, let's call them that. I can give you his name, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, it doesn't really matter. I suppose to the person who is sitting here today?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ever since then, in Sarajevo and in the federation, some people, Bosniaks, learned that I had got in touch with your Defence team and then I was supposed to be liquidated, and I mentioned it in my statement. What I've seen so far from the Prosecutor, all that was rigged by Damir Alagic in the federation, he's the one who produced this newspaper article because there was a question at that time as to what to do with me and where to send me. I got a paper from the Kosevo hospital where Damir Alagic took me in order for the doctors to proclaim me insane, and when the main doctor in the hospital arrived and a lady doctor with him and when they realised that I was not insane, they wouldn't admit me. I have a paper proving what they did at the hospital to me on that day. Ever since then, I was on the street until I was found by that man whom I mentioned in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With the Trial Chamber's leave, I would like to ask you to send us a copy of that paper, testifying to their attempt to hospitalise you at the psychiatric ward. You said earlier today that you had left of your own accord to the newspaper. Did you ever go to a newspaper of your own will?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, as far as what newspapers write, Damir Alagic is the one who should be here and tell you eyeball to eyeball how they rigged that article.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then Damir Alagic called you and told you that The Hague Tribunal was looking for you. Did he tell you why The Hague Tribunal was looking for you?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not tell me why. He just called me and told me this: The Hague is looking for you. If they find you, don't talk to them before I come. I will deal with it. I will be the one doing all the talking. He told me that on the phone, and after that, perhaps three days later, I received news from my father who is in Tuzla that I received a threat from a group of Naser's men and that I could not come back home. I had to disappear. I came to the town where I was born and the civilian police there helped me because he knew the story. I would like to call the head of the civilian police there as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us which of the Tribunal's services was looking for you at the time?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't tell you. I don't know. You're talking about Damir Alagic? I really don't know. He only told me that The Hague was looking for me. He says, The Hague is looking for you. If The Hague finds you, don't talk to them until I arrive. I don't know who was looking for me. And, Mr. President, they know that The Hague was looking for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will ask the Registry to find out and inform us who it was that was looking for you. And the interview in the prison, your first interview, was it recorded? Did you say everything literally or was it typed while you were talking or was it hand recorded? Are you the one who worded things the way they were recorded or is it somebody else who did that?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please explain? Are you talking about my letter when they arrived from Sarajevo or about your defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When they came to visit you, Kulovac, for example.

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything was recorded on computer and on DVD.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when was that downloaded and typed on paper? When did you sign that?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was on the same day when I went to the bathroom. That -- I signed that and then the policeman protected me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you say only what is written there or did somebody actually formulate your words for you?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What the Prosecution presented as my statement on paper and my signature, that should have been completed in the Prosecutor's office in Sarajevo during the Defence case of those six guys from Sarajevo. Bajro Kulovac did not invite me as a witness, the document was removed, and those guys received sentences of up to 30 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 60 earlier today a mention was made on the -- of the killing of your mother and son. There was a slight confusion there. I would like to call up on the ELMO a document which shouldn't be broadcast. We need to see the first and the last pages in that document. Please do not mention your father's name. It has been suggested that your son -- your father had also witnessed the killing of your mother and son. Can we first see the first page? Don't give us the name. Could you just tell us who that person is and whether he told the truth about the event? This should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I've got this in English. Perhaps it would be better so everyone could see it and we've got in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: The document that is being shown on the ELMO, I have it in English and B/C/S and in e-court, so it might be easier just to use that. Can I suggest that that is uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have it in English?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, it's uploaded and it has got a translation, yeah. Yes, Your Honour. If I just find the 65 ter number, it won't take me a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 25505. And it obviously shouldn't be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Don't tell us the name, just tell us who the man is and how you are related to him, if you are. The third line from the bottom of the page where it says "witness."

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know him. And I want to tell you now very publicly, when the Prosecutor asked me about that, I said that I had heard from this man here that he was visited by some Prosecutors and they asked him about the murder of my mother and son, and he did not want to provide a correct statement to them because he didn't want to get involved. And from the moment he provided his statement, the people at the top denied everything that I said based on his words, and I would like to tell everybody here whatever the Prosecutor presented today is what I said myself, if I can remember it well. I'm now addressing the main co-ordinator to find that recording. When I first met him, I told him that I did not want this man to be sentenced for this, to be convicted for this, because -- because his younger brother saved my life. I know that at the very beginning I said to your main co-ordinator what had happened. I did not want this man to suffer because his brother saved my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see the last page, or rather the sixth page? Paragraph 11. It will be easier. Can you see that he says here that he asked you where she was, you said she had come out to the first floor with the child in her arms, that Pasan [phoen] and Pasan's family were recorded as missing, that Pasan's family was found, that the others were not, that was in 2009; is this correct? He says: As far as my wife's and grandson's fates are concerned, I didn't see exactly what had happened to them.

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I told Madam Prosecutor that he was not able to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So as far as this matter is concerned, the statement is correct?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement where he says he hadn't seen the murder of his wife and grandson, that's true. He wasn't able to see. But the process, the proceedings that are now going on in the federation and Republika Srpska you can see that he went to court with two witnesses, and those two witnesses giving a statement before the Court said in his defence that they had seen that the Chetniks had thrown grenades through the window, killing my mother and son. And based on his statement before the Court, there are papers in the house, all the property was signed over to him, and I was recorded as dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this Ejub Zukic the same one that signed your statement?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ejub Zukic. Possibly. I don't know the man. The man who gave the statement should tell you with whom he was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Just before -- in case Dr. Karadzic is about to leave this document, I think in fairness, that the entire of that paragraph 12 should be read because it's only been partially summarised, and there is more to it than what was read out. And for the record, if it's not sought to admit that then I would ask that -- preferably 11 and 12 but certainly 12 is read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Without reading out the real names?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to do that?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, of course. And just with perhaps a little bit of 11: As far as the fate of my wife and grandson are concerned, I did not see exactly what happened to them. Last time I saw her was before I left the cellar to light a cigarette and she remained inside. When I returned the witness told me that she had gone upstairs and that she had carried my grandson in her arms. I know that after that, we were -- I know that after we were taken to the stadium, the women were left behind in the village, describes the women, all of them and my wife and my grandson, all of them are registered as missing. As far as I know -- it goes on, paragraph 12: After getting to Visoko and later on to Zivinice, I kept searching for my wife. As soon as I learned that some refugees arrived from Bratunac, I would go to look for my wife and grandson. I inquired about them. My son, the witness, was also asking around about the fates of my wife and my grandson and he never once mentioned that my wife was killed. I know that my son, the witness, went to Srebrenica, et cetera. Goes on. I just wanted to make sure that the full record is read. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you allow me for just one second because I now only saw what's written here. I want to refute the statement of this man. That woman and that child were not in the basement. I invite the witness Muhamed Ahmetovic who lives here in Holland. My mother and son were not in the basement. They were upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There was a number of people in the basement. Why were they in the basement?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 10th of May, 1992, when the shooting started from those hills all around Bratunac, Kik, Susko Brdo, Gornica [phoen], we went into hiding in the basement because bullets were hitting the roof and tiles were falling off, so we hid in the basement and my mother and son remained upstairs. They were not in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's clarify this. How many experts have talked to you? One or two? During the first examination ordered by the Court, how many psychiatrists have spoken to you?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just want to understand, in which case, which experts, because as you know well, there are two or three cases in which I'm involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In 1996, when the investigating judge asked that you be examined by an expert, and we saw that document, it was almost illegible, how many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only one, that forensic expert from Serbia, who reappeared again when the retrial was going on. He told the Court how I had come to be in Zvornik and all that had gone on. Nebojsa Jovanovic denied that I was beaten in Zvornik, that I was mistreated by the police, and the Prosecutor, Nebojsa Ivanovic, therefore asked for a new examination by a new expert. Then I was taken to Banja Luka to be seen by a new expert, but the expert in Banja Luka did not agree with his own colleague from 1996, the good man who had seen me and who came to my retrial, the man who had seen in 1996 that I was a broken man. So since the two of them could not agree, they invited a third expert, a woman, who claimed that I only want to be acquitted, freed, in order to appear here, in order to be able to come here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Am I understanding you correctly that there are three forensic reports in that whole process which started in 1996?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this first case, when the first expert examined you, were some tests done? How long was the interview and what were these tests?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to make you understand one thing. The man comes to see you in an office, he asks for some personal details, then he reads the judgement and then he appears before the Court and he says, You are guilty of this and that and that, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In that report, it is written that there were two of them and that they applied four tests, including one that I know very well, MMPI, but they did not apply the IQ test, although they made a finding on your intellect. Did they perform any tests?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. In no place wherever I met those three experts, including the one from Serbia who knew my case in 1996, the one in Banja Luka and the woman who came to my trial, I never saw them all together, only one by one, and they read my judgement and they took my judgement into court and testified in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us, did you give a statement to some judicial institution in Belgrade? Were you questioned by the judiciary in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is this about?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: About all these events, about all that you know. Were you questioned before a Judge or a Prosecutor in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a bogus trial, and a false conviction, and that's why I begged all these Prosecutors and lawyers and Judges to find me a lawyer who would institute this procedure immediately, urgently, because I can't tell you -- I can't get over it that I had been in prison for nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In that interview, did you speak about the events in Sarajevo? And did you tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One hundred per cent. And I swear on everything that is most sacred to me, but the people in that Prosecutor's office and the Judges could not understand what I was saying for a long time until we went out into the field in Republika Srpska. I had been drawing them maps to show them where things were, and I gave them statements, I drew places and scenes and sometimes we worked days and nights with these Prosecutors and Judges and investigators, but when we finally came to the scene, they couldn't believe how exact my maps were. Every stone, every rock, was exactly drawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that you had offered Serbian authorities and representatives -- that you could show them some mass graves of the Serbs. Are there any that are still unidentified, mass graves of Serbs and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: KW12 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said yesterday. I asked this International Tribunal to approve that we go to the federation, to the crime scenes, Hajvazi primarily, that's the one that interests me the most because there must be evidence there, because when we went to those locations, the federation authorities did not allow us to go there. They did not guarantee our security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, that concludes your evidence, Mr. Witness. On behalf of the Chamber, I'd like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go. But please remain seated. We will rise all together. We will rise for five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, can we go on maybe till 3.00 today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will discuss it when we return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: --- Break taken at 2.29 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we continue, can I hear from you about the witness schedule for this week, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Because we have a lot of witnesses here this week, we've asked some of those who are not in a hurry that they have to go home to stay a little bit longer, and so we are skipping some of the witnesses that we had originally planned earlier in the week. So this is Mr. Matovic in front of you, and he will testify today and probably continue tomorrow morning. At which point the next witness will be Mr. Milicic and then Mr. Kovacevic. If we have sometime tomorrow, we can begin the testimony of Mr. Radikovic. But on Thursday at 9.00 a.m., we need to start and conclude the testimony of Colonel Blagojevic. And then we need to have the testimony -- the direct examination of General Tolimir on Thursday. And, as a result of that, Mr. Miskovic, who was scheduled for earlier this week, will now be testifying next week and Radikovic will continue his testimony next week if he begins it at all tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we need to revise the subpoena for General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't believe so. We filed a notice that it's to be on the 12th and his legal adviser is here and ready to proceed, so I don't think that anything further is necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Today we need to rise at least five or ten to 3.00 given that the Judges have a plenary today. Would the witness make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall I begin? I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Matovic. Please be seated and make yourself comfortable. Going back to the schedule, Mr. Robinson, there is no need for the Chamber to sit on Friday?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Matovic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR MATOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask you to leave a short pause between my questions and your answers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Whether it's important or not, I note that, Mr. Matovic, you are the 200th Defence witness for this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With Mr. Matovic, there is always some round figure. Have you given a statement to the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR MATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D09095 is the document I would like to call up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see your statement before you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR MATOVIC
utterances.text: I'll need my glasses. I see it, but not well enough to read. But, I know approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you read and signed that statement?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR MATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the last page, in the Serbian?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR MATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this statement faithfully reflect what you said?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR MATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I were to put to you the same questions today, would your answers be essentially the same as recorded in the statement?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR MATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this statement under -- your Excellencies, under 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any objection, Ms. Edgerton, to admit this pursuant to Rule 92 ter?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives Exhibit D4184, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will read a very short summary of Mr. Matovic's statement and then I'll have a couple of questions for him. [In English] Vladimir Matovic was a long-term journalist for "Borba" magazine in Belgrade and an adviser to former president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Dobrica Cosic. In July 1995, former President Cosic and others in Serbia became concerned that the international community would use the Bosnian Serbs' military action in the Srebrenica area as a justification for military action against the Serbs. At the request of former President Cosic, Mr. Matovic travelled to Srebrenica area in July 1995 where he witnessed the large number of Bosnian Muslims who had gathered at Potocari. He proceeded to Pale where he met with President Karadzic. Mr. Matovic states that from his conversation with President Karadzic on that occasion, it was clear to him that President Karadzic was not well-informed concerning the events in Srebrenica. It seemed to Mr. Matovic that President Karadzic was getting his information about the Srebrenica events from CNN. Mr. Matovic returned to Pale a few days later to deliver a letter written by President Cosic and Patriarch Pavle. To the best of his recollection, he did not see President Karadzic on this occasion but left the letter with a secretary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'd like, Mr. Matovic, to ask you to tell us whether you were close enough to President Cosic while he was president and later until the end of our war?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR MATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he invited me to join his team. I left my job as a journalist. I joined his office. I was a press officer for 90 days, and since I knew him, I had known him for a long time, and I sided with him always in the public, although he was not always very popular in the public eye because President Cosic was a renowned writer, a huge number of books printed in a very large circulation and translated into many languages. He was a writer who wrote about the national tragedies of Serbs through various wars. Briefly he was a prominent author, and one of his books is the title, "The Serbian Issue - Democratic Issue."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of his attitude to Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR MATOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, especially since I started working with him, and even before, while I was working as a journalist, I had to deal with this issue and keep myself abreast and I was familiar with his position and opinions. And after one conversation I had with Alija Izetbegovic, I conveyed to Cosic the gist of that conversation, and Alija Izetbegovic had served time in prison in Sarajevo, I'm trying to tell this briefly, to give you the shortened version, anyway I conveyed to Cosic that it was a big question because the ruling party in Sarajevo and their newspaper, "Oslobodjenje," wanted to print an interview --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please do not overlap because you are speaking -- both of you are speaking the same language. You should put a pause between the question and answer. But before we ask you to repeat, yes, Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, I was waiting, Your Honours, to see where this was going, a bit concerned as to whether or not we were about to hear some kind of attestation on behalf of President Cosic because none of that is in the statement that this witness signed, at all. And if this goes my further, we have a notice issue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't -- I don't intend to repeat anything from the statement. I just wanted to ask the witness if he was aware of the emotional and other position of Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, the issue was the notice to the Prosecution of the subject matter of the witness's evidence. Mr. Robinson, can you assist us?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, not really, Mr. President. I was present at the proofing, but I didn't see that this was coming up so I don't really know exactly what Dr. Karadzic is seeking to elicit here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How much longer do you need to conclude your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One minute. It depends on the answer. All I want to know is what he knew about President Cosic's altitude towards Muslims and my own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He answered the first question. Yes. Your second question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A second question: Do you know what President Cosic thought about my attitude to the Muslims? How did he see me?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR MATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's a difficult question because his relationship with you -- I don't know whether it was friendly, harmonious, but in that whole Serbian environment after the establishment of the council, the board, in Belgrade, which was the opposition to the then-government, established a forum to protect freedom of speech. And since he heard that Mr. Izetbegovic had been arrested and he was about to be tried because of his position on religion and his public statements, he put it before the Belgrade association and put forward his position which was very courageous at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you just answer the question: How did President Cosic see my attitude to the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR MATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he always had only the nicest things to say about you. He spoke of you as a prominent poet, intellectual, psychiatrist, et cetera, et cetera. And on most political issues, including that one, he spoke of you very well, saying that you were one of the people in Sarajevo and in Bosnia-Herzegovina as a whole who was seen as a leader of the Serbs. He saw you as somebody who shared his views that nobody should be arrested for any kind of public statement, and Izetbegovic's wife came, together with a delegation of the families of all those who were arrested because of that Islamic Declaration, she brought a lot of money --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's enough for now because that's not in the statement. That's why I wanted it on record. Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Matovic, we will adjourn here for today and continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. Tomorrow morning you will be cross-examined by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor, but while you are giving testimony, I would like to advise you not to discuss about your testimony with anybody else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 11th day of December, 2013, at 9.00 a.m. 25
